To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• We consider a possible ‘worst case’ scenario of SUSY with a compressed spectrum, where the gluino, squarks and the lightest SUS-Y particle (LSP) are all degenerate.

(i) The current limits on the gluino and squark masses are reduced by up to a factor of two for compressed spectra, (ii) The most sensitive searches to compressed spectra are those with the LSPs recoilling against ISR, (iii) Matching and shower uncertainties are signicantly reduced by the CKKW-L matching procedure, (iv) The CMS monojet analysis is the most sensitive monojet search to date.

the study of supersymmetry (or SUSY) in the light of recent experimental results from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).
the theoretical aspects of the production and decay of supersymmetric particles.
the theoretical understanding of the LHC searches for SUSY with compressed spectra.

compressed spectra are still viable and that current limits from the Lhc are not yet strong enough to rule out such scenarios.

the LHC has not yet excluded a compressed spectrum scenario where the LSP is a neutralino and all other SUSY states are heavier than about 500 GeV, with the exception of a light stau which is allowed to be as light as 150 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current LHC searches for compressed spectra are extremely robust and can be trusted to give accurate results.
the current LHC searches are very sensitive to compressed spectra and can be used to constrain SUSY models with a compressed spectrum.
the current limits on compressed spectra are much weaker than previously thought.
